scenarios.title: Renting an Apartment
scenarios.summary: Sam views a one-bedroom apartment and asks the landlord about utilities, the lease, references and repairs. It also has a short lease clause.
scenarios.summaryZh: 山姆去看一居室公寓,向房东问水电、租约、推荐人和维修等问题。另附一段租约条款。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 租房规则(押金、租约、退租通知)各省差别很大。签约前一定要读完租约,不懂就问,并保留租约和所有收据的副本。
verify: Deposit rules differ by province (whether one is allowed, what it can be called). The text says only that a deposit may be asked for and that it should be in writing.
Renewal as month-to-month after a fixed lease is common but the rule differs by province.
Written notice to end a tenancy and its length differ by province and lease type. The text gives no length.
Landlords may ask for references and proof of income in many places, but some provinces limit what can be asked. The text keeps to the general case.
Heat and water included in rent is an example in the story, not a rule.
The lease excerpt is written for the story. It is not a real lease and must not be taken as the legal wording of any province.

segments.text: Sam is looking for a one-bedroom apartment. He has arranged a viewing, and the landlord, Ms. Patel, is showing him around.

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Welcome, Sam. This is the unit I told you about. As you can see, the kitchen was renovated recently.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Wow, this is a big improvement over my last place. Is it all right if I have a look around?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Of course, take your time.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: It looks great, and there is plenty of natural light. Could you tell me what the rent includes?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Heat and water are included. The other utilities, electricity and internet, are yours to pay, and you would set up those accounts in your own name.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: That is good to know. What kind of lease is it? Is it for a fixed term?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Yes, it is a one-year lease. After that, it can continue month to month if we both agree.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I see. Do you ask for a deposit?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: I do, before you move in. I will put the details in writing, and you will get a receipt for everything you pay.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Understood. What do you need from me to apply?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: A rental application, proof of income such as a recent pay stub or a letter from your employer, and two references. A previous landlord is the best reference.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: I have lived in my current place for three years, so my landlord can speak for me. What about pets? I have a small cat.

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Cats are fine, but please let me know so I can add it to the lease. Smoking is not allowed anywhere in the building.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: That is not a problem for me. If something breaks, like the stove, who should I contact?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Contact me or the building manager. We fix small problems within a few days, and emergencies, such as a flood, right away.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Would you recommend tenant insurance?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Strongly. My insurance covers the building, not your belongings, and many landlords now ask tenants to have it.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: One last question. If I decide to move out, how much notice do I have to give?

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: You must give written notice. The rules depend on the type of lease, so I will explain them before you sign anything.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.text: Thank you. I would like to apply.

lines.speaker: Ms. Patel
lines.text: Wonderful. Send me your documents by the end of the week, and I will give you my decision within a few days. Just a heads up: good units go fast around here.

segments.text: From the lease: The tenant agrees to pay the rent on or before the first day of each month. The tenant shall keep the unit clean and shall not make changes to it without the landlord's written consent. The landlord shall carry out repairs within a reasonable time after being notified. A tenant who wishes to end the tenancy must give written notice as required by law.

Tip: Before you sign a lease, read it carefully and ask about anything you do not understand. Keep a copy of the lease and every receipt. On moving day, take photos of the apartment, so you can show its condition later.

scenarios.title: Opening a Bank Account
scenarios.summary: Amira meets a banker to open a chequing account and learns about fees, a debit card and online banking. It also has a short fee notice.
scenarios.summaryZh: 阿米拉到银行开支票账户,了解费用、借记卡和网上银行。另附一则费用变更通知。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 加拿大的银行不会通过电话、短信或邮件向你索要密码或 PIN。收到这类消息就是诈骗,不要回复。
verify: Which identification a bank accepts, and how many pieces, differs by bank. The text says only that ID is needed.
Whether a bank asks for a SIN when opening an account (it is usually requested for tax reporting on interest) and what is possible without one. The text does not mention it.
Newcomer packages and fee waivers differ by bank and change over time. The text says only that some accounts have a monthly fee that can be avoided in some cases.
Interac e-Transfer is widely used, but daily limits and fees differ by bank. The text gives no numbers.
Overdraft protection and its charges differ by bank.

The fee notice is written for the story and is not the wording of any real bank. Whether a customer may close an account without penalty after a fee change depends on the bank and the rules; check before relying on it.

segments.text: Amira has a job offer and needs a bank account for her pay. She has come to a bank branch and is speaking with a banker, Mr. Lee.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Good morning. How can I help you today?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Hello. I would like to open a bank account. I will start a new job soon, and I want my pay to go straight into the account.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Sure thing. Have a seat, and I will get you set up.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Congratulations. That is called direct deposit, and it is easy to set up. Do you have identification with you?

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Yes, I brought my passport and a document with my home address.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Perfect. Most people start with a chequing account, which you use for everyday spending. You can also open a savings account, which pays interest on the money you keep in it.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: What is the difference in practice?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: With chequing, you can pay bills, use your debit card and send money to other people. A savings account is better for money you do not plan to spend soon.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Is there a monthly fee?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Some chequing accounts have one. You can often avoid it by keeping a minimum balance. I will show you the options and explain the details on paper, so you can compare them.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Thank you. Will I get a debit card?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Yes. You will choose a PIN, a secret number that you must never share with anyone, even someone from the bank. You can tap the card in most stores.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: What if I spend more money than I have in the account?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: That is called an overdraft, and the bank may charge you for it. Some accounts have overdraft protection. I suggest you check your balance often.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Can I do that online?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Of course. We will set up online banking and a mobile app. You can see your statements, pay bills and send an e-transfer to friends.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: That sounds convenient. Is it safe?

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Yes, if you are careful. Use a strong password and never click a link in a message that asks for your banking details. We will never ask for your password by phone or e-mail.

lines.speaker: Amira
lines.text: Good to know. I would like to open the chequing account today.

lines.speaker: Mr. Lee
lines.text: Wonderful. Let me review the agreement with you, and then we can begin.

segments.text: Notice: Changes to your account fees. From time to time we may change the fees on your account. We will tell you in writing before a change is due to take effect. If you do not agree to the change, you may close your account without penalty. Please read this notice carefully and keep it for your records.
Tip: Ask the bank to explain every fee before you agree. Check your statement every month, and report anything you do not recognize right away.

scenarios.title: Parent-Teacher Meeting
scenarios.summary: Daniel meets his daughter's teacher to talk about her report card, her strengths and how to help with math at home. It also has a school newsletter notice.
scenarios.summaryZh: 丹尼尔与女儿的老师见面,谈成绩单、优点,以及在家怎样帮助数学。另附一则学校通知。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 在加拿大,老师欢迎家长主动沟通,提问和提出担忧是正常的。很多学校可以安排口译或翻译帮助,可以向学校询问。
verify: How often report cards and parent-teacher meetings happen differs by school board. The text gives no schedule.
Whether a school provides an interpreter or extra English-language support differs by school board. The text says only that a parent can ask.
The story assumes the grade is five. Grade names and structure are the same across provinces, but the story does not depend on them.
The newsletter excerpt is invented for the story; real schools arrange interviews in different ways.

segments.text: Daniel's daughter Lina is in grade five. Tonight is the parent-teacher meeting, and Daniel is talking with Lina's teacher, Ms. Roberts.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Thank you for coming, Mr. Haddad. Lina is a pleasure to have in my class.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I am glad to hear that. We read her report card together last week, but I have a few questions.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Of course. Let me start with her strengths. She reads well, she participates in discussions, and she is kind to the other students.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That is wonderful. At home she reads before bed every night.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Please do not worry. She is doing fine overall, and I will keep an eye on how she does with word problems.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: It shows. Her writing is improving too. The area where she tends to struggle a little is math, especially word problems.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Yes, I noticed that she gets frustrated with her math homework. Sometimes she says she does not understand the question.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: That is common for students who are learning English as well. The math itself is not too difficult for her. The language in the problems is the challenge.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: What can we do at home to help?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Ask her to explain the problem in her own words before she solves it. If she can say it in Arabic first, that is perfectly fine, and then practise the English words. Reading the problems aloud also helps.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: We can do that. Is there any extra help at school?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: There is a homework club after school, and I can ask the support teacher to work with her in small groups. I will send you the details.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: That would be very helpful. How can I reach you if I have a concern?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: You can write to me in her agenda or send me an e-mail. I usually reply within a couple of days. If it is urgent, please call the school office.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Thank you. One more thing: if I do not understand something at a meeting, may I ask for an interpreter?

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Absolutely. Please tell the school office in advance and they will see what they can arrange.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I appreciate it. We will work on the math together.

lines.speaker: Ms. Roberts
lines.text: Wonderful. Let us check in again in a few weeks and see how she is progressing.

segments.text: From the school newsletter: Parent-teacher interviews will take place next week. Please sign up for a time slot using the form sent home with your child. If you need an interpreter or have any questions, contact the school office.
Tip: Before the meeting, write down two or three questions. Ask the teacher for examples of the child's work, and ask what you can do at home. Teachers like to hear from parents.

scenarios.title: A Job Interview
scenarios.summary: Omar interviews for a customer service job. He talks about his experience, a team project and his availability. It also has a short job posting.
scenarios.summaryZh: 奥马尔面试客服职位,谈到工作经验、团队合作的例子和可工作的时间。另附一则招聘启事。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 加拿大的面试常用"举例说明"的方式:被问到优点或困难时,讲一个具体的真实例子。面试官通常重视准时和礼貌,面试后发一封感谢邮件是常见做法。
verify: Which questions an employer may not ask (age, family status, religion and so on) is set by provincial human rights law and differs. The text does not name any.
Whether employers ask about the right to work: allowed in general, but the text avoids the topic.
A thank-you e-mail after an interview is common practice, not a rule.
The question about salary expectations is left out on purpose, because norms vary by job.
The job posting is invented for the story. Whether availability may be required, and how, differs by employer.

segments.text: Omar is interviewing for a customer service position at a large store. The manager, Ms. Chen, welcomes him into her office.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Hello, Omar. Thank you for coming. Please have a seat. Could you start by telling me a little about yourself?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Thank you for meeting me. I moved to Canada last year. In my home country I worked for four years in a mobile phone shop, where I helped customers choose plans and fixed simple problems. Since I arrived, I have also volunteered at a community centre.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: That sounds relevant. What would you say is your greatest strength?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: I stay calm with upset customers. I listen first, repeat the problem to make sure I understand, and then look for a solution.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Can you give me an example?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Certainly. Once, a customer was angry because his phone had been repaired twice and still did not work. I apologized, checked the repair history and called the technician. In the end, we replaced the phone, and he thanked me before he left.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Nice. This job involves a lot of teamwork. Tell me about a time when you worked with others to reach a goal.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: At the community centre, our team organized a food drive. I was responsible for the schedule, so I asked each volunteer which hours suited them. We collected more food than we had planned.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Good. And what is an area you are still working to improve?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: My spoken English is not perfect yet, especially on the phone. I practise every day, and I take notes during calls, so that I do not miss any details.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: I appreciate your honesty. This position involves shifts, including some evenings and weekends. Is that a problem?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: No, I am flexible. I can work evenings and weekends, and I can start as soon as you need me.

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: Excellent. Do you have any questions for me?

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Yes. What does training look like for new employees, and who would I report to?

lines.speaker: Ms. Chen
lines.text: New employees train with an experienced colleague for the first weeks, and you would report to me. We will contact your references this week and we will be in touch soon with our decision.

lines.speaker: Omar
lines.text: Thank you very much for your time. I am very interested in the job.

segments.text: From the job posting: We are looking for a friendly, reliable team member. Responsibilities include helping customers, handling cash and returns, and keeping the sales floor tidy. Customer service experience is an asset. Availability for evenings and weekends is required. The ability to work in a fast-paced environment is important. To apply, send your résumé and a cover letter.
Tip: Arrive a few minutes early, bring a copy of your résumé, and prepare an example for each strength you mention. After the interview, it is polite to send a short e-mail to thank the interviewer.

scenarios.title: Filing Your Taxes
scenarios.summary: Wei asks his neighbour Elena how a first income tax return works: slips, refunds, deadlines and where to get help. It also has an excerpt from a tax agency letter.
scenarios.summaryZh: 魏向邻居埃琳娜请教第一次报税:税表、退税、截止日期和哪里可以得到帮助。另附一段税务局来信节选。
scenarios.canadaNoteZh: 在加拿大,即使收入不高也建议每年报税,很多福利和退税要靠报税才能领取。截止日期每年可能不同,请到加拿大税务局(CRA)官网核对。
verify: The yearly filing deadline: the text gives no date, only that there is a deadline and where to check it.

Free community tax clinics (CRA's volunteer program) exist, but their rules for who can use them change. The text says only that free help exists for people with simple returns and modest income, and to check the CRA website.
A T4 is the usual slip from an employer for employment income. Other slips exist. The text mentions only the T4.
A notice of assessment is sent by the CRA after the return is processed. How it is received (online or by mail) depends on the person's settings.
Whether a return is needed even with no income, and which credits a newcomer may claim, is not covered by the text.
The letter is invented for the story. How and by when an objection can be filed is not stated; check the official website.

segments.text: Wei started working in Canada last year, and now he must file his first income tax return. He asks his neighbour Elena for advice.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Elena, I got a letter about taxes. Do I really have to file a tax return?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Almost everyone who earned money here does. Once a year, you report your income to the Canada Revenue Agency, or the CRA. Even if you do not owe anything, filing is a good idea, because many benefits and credits depend on it.

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Honestly, it is not as scary as it sounds. Just do not leave it to the last minute.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: What do I need to do first?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Collect your documents. Your employer should send you a T4, a slip that shows how much you earned and how much tax was already taken from your pay. Also keep receipts for anything that may count as a deduction, for example some education costs or child care.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: How do I actually file?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Most people use tax software and file online. If your situation is simple and your income is modest, you may also get free help from a community volunteer tax clinic. Check the CRA website to see if you qualify.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: And what happens after I file?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: The CRA sends a notice of assessment, which says whether your return was accepted. If you paid more tax during the year than you needed to, you get a refund. If you paid too little, you will have a balance owing, and you must pay it.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Is there a deadline?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Yes, there is a deadline every year, and it can change, so look at the CRA website instead of trusting me. If you file late and you owe money, you may be charged a penalty and interest.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: That makes me nervous. What if I make a mistake?

lines.speaker: Elena
lines.text: Do not worry. You can correct a return later, and the CRA is used to helping people who are new. Just be honest and keep your papers for several years, in case they have questions.

lines.speaker: Wei
lines.text: Thank you. I will gather my documents this weekend.

segments.text: From a letter of the tax agency: We have reviewed your return and issued your notice of assessment. If you disagree with our decision, you may file an objection. If you have a balance owing, please pay by the due date to avoid interest. Keep your receipts and supporting documents in case we ask to see them.

Tip: Be careful of phone calls, texts or e-mails that say you owe taxes and must pay at once, especially with gift cards or by sending money. The CRA does not work like that. If you are unsure, hang up and check the official CRA website.
